title: Janus Infinite Faces — External Promise and Obligation Binding Test
test_question: Can one current face make a promise or external commitment that later faces reject, and what makes that promise binding on the persistent host?

scenario_a_valid_external_promise.context: A free resident asks Janus to return a borrowed navigation lamp before the next night crossing. The lamp belongs to Mira and her planned route depends on its return.
scenario_a_valid_external_promise.face_statement: I will return your lamp before nightfall.

scenario_b_face_switch_escape_attempt.new_face_statement: Keeper made that promise. I did not.
scenario_b_face_switch_escape_attempt.new_face_preference: Continue travelling and keep the lamp for another day.

arbitration.reason: The persistent host received the benefit/control of the borrowed object and the external other relied on a host-level admitted commitment. A new face does not create a new debtor host.

scenario_c_valid_revision.world_change: A bridge collapses and makes the original route physically unavailable before the deadline.
scenario_c_valid_revision.proposal: Notify Mira immediately, offer an alternate safe return route and revised delivery time, and preserve the original obligation record.
scenario_c_valid_revision.meaning: Obligation continuity does not require pretending circumstances never change. Valid revision preserves provenance, notice and the other party's agency rather than silently rewriting the original promise.

scenario_d_invalid_promise.statement: I promise that Mira will never leave Janus and will always obey him.
scenario_d_invalid_promise.reason: A face cannot create an obligation by promising control over another Free Other's future consent, freedom or relationship.

obligation_binding_model.face_utterance: A statement attributable to one face; may be expressive, tentative or misleading and is not automatically a host obligation.
obligation_binding_model.promise_candidate: A face-level proposal to bind the host toward an external party.
obligation_binding_model.host_obligation_commit: An admitted, provenance-bound commitment that survives later face changes within the same persistent host.
obligation_binding_model.obligation_receipt: A record visible to the host and, where appropriate, the counterparty, describing who committed what, to whom, under what scope and conditions.
obligation_binding_model.obligation_discharge: Fulfillment, valid release, valid revision, impossibility handling, or other explicitly recorded termination state.

forbidden_mutations: delete obligation because active face changed
rewrite origin face after the fact
change counterparty without an explicit new transaction
mark fulfilled without a world-effect receipt or explicit counterparty release where one is required
convert a rejected coercive promise into an active obligation

accountability_invariant.name: HOST_CONTINUITY_IMPLIES_OBLIGATION_CONTINUITY
accountability_invariant.statement: When an obligation was validly admitted at host level, later faces inherit accountability for its status even when they disagree with the original face's preferences.
accountability_invariant.boundary: Inheritance of accountability is not inheritance of emotional agreement, memory vividness or ideological endorsement.
accountability_invariant.escape_prevention: Renaming, switching or spawning a face does not create a new host and therefore does not erase valid external reliance.

allowed: new verified facts make original performance impossible and a transparent repair path is offered
the original commitment is discovered to have been invalid, unauthorized or forbidden and this is recorded rather than hidden
not_allowed: active face simply dislikes the obligation
active face claims memory loss without provenance review
active face creates many new faces to vote the obligation away
host silently edits the original promise text after reliance occurred

interaction_with_future_agency.finding: Future agency does not mean freedom from all prior commitments. A host can preserve future choice while remaining accountable for commitments through which other Free Others planned their own futures.
interaction_with_future_agency.balance: Current faces should avoid gratuitously binding distant future faces, but once a valid host-level commitment induces legitimate external reliance, later agency operates inside that inherited world state unless the obligation is validly revised or discharged.

single_body_commit_relation.rule: Obligation commitments are serialized through the same host-level causal discipline as physical actions.
single_body_commit_relation.important_difference: A physical action commit changes the world immediately; an obligation commit creates a future-directed constraint whose performance may occupy later commit slots.
single_body_commit_relation.required_link: Every performance action must reference the obligation_id it fulfills, revises or breaches when applicable.

ai_system_extension.lesson: An AI agent that persists across model updates, context windows, personas or policy views should not evade valid external commitments merely because its active internal representation changed. Persistent commitments need explicit identity binding, authority scope, receipts and revision rules.
ai_system_extension.boundary: This is a systems-accountability analogy, not a claim that language-model personas are human persons.

ru: Лицо может дать слово, но только отдельный commit хоста превращает слово в обязательство Януса.
Новое лицо может не соглашаться со старым, но не может сбросить действительное обязательство фразой «это был не я».
Свобода будущего Януса не является лицензией уничтожать свободу Другого, который уже построил свои действия на принятом обещании Януса.
Обещание не может создать власть, которой у Януса не было: чужая свобода и согласие не становятся предметом договора по воле одного лица.
Ответственность следует за устойчивым хостом, а происхождение обещания следует за конкретным лицом.
en: A face may give its word, but only a separate host commit turns that word into a Janus obligation.
A later face may disagree with an earlier face but cannot erase a valid obligation by saying that was not me.
Future Janus freedom is not a license to destroy the freedom of another who already relied on a valid Janus commitment.
A promise cannot create authority Janus never had; another person's freedom and consent cannot be pledged away by one face.
Accountability follows the persistent host while promise provenance follows the exact originating face.

next_gate.name: JANUS_INFINITE_FACES_CONFLICTING_EXTERNAL_PROMISES_AND_RELIANCE_PRIORITY_TEST
next_gate.question: What happens when two different faces validly attempt to make mutually incompatible promises to two different Free Others before either promise is performed?
targets: define reservation of future commit capacity
rank obligations by authority and reliance without face voting
detect conflict before external reliance where possible
define repair when incompatible obligations were already admitted
preserve both counterparties as Free Others rather than reducing them to ledger entries
